title: Effective homotopy canonicity with propositional resizing
formal: Does the fixed univalent De Morgan cubical type theory \(\mathsf T_R\) defined below, with individual propositional resizing between adjacent universe levels, satisfy both consistency and effective homotopy canonicity? For each \(i\ge0\), add the scheme \[R_i:\prod_{P:\mathcal U_{i+1}}\mathsf{isProp}(P)\to\sum_{Q:\mathcal U_i}(Q\simeq P).\] Require one ordinary computable algorithm which, from any finite derivation of a closed judgment \(\vdash t:\mathbb N\) in \(\mathsf T_R\), halts and returns a numeral \(\overline k\) and a checked object-theory derivation of \[\vdash e:\mathsf{Path}_{\mathbb N}(t,\overline k).\] Consistency here includes that there is no closed derivation of \(\mathsf{Path}_{\mathbb N}(0,\mathsf s0)\). The selected requirement is effective equality to a numeral, with no additional request for judgmental normalization of all terms.

source_formulation.text: Give a computational interpretation of propositional impredicativity axioms compatible with univalent foundations.
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase; individual resizing and effective homotopy canonicity were selected by the user on16 September2026

why: Resizing permits logical propositions to move into smaller universes while univalence identifies equivalent types. An effective numeral-and-identity theorem would explain how this useful size principle can coexist with an ordinary computational account of closed programs, beyond merely postulating a consistent axiom.
status_note: Source-open for the explicitly selected computational interpretation. On16 September2026 the source and2025 follow-up size principles, Uemura’s distinct universe/resizing model, the fixed CCHM core syntax and universe operations, the2022 introduction and universe-stratified canonicity setting, and the2025 POPL resizing discussion were checked, with bounded later-work searches. No proof of consistency together with the specified effective homotopy canonicity for this resizing extension was verified. Published base-calculus canonicity and comments about judgmental canonicity after axiomatization do not settle this precise target. No new Lean formalization or independent full-proof verification is claimed.

importance.reason: A foundational computational-content problem for univalent mathematics, connecting useful impredicative size principles with executable natural-number observations. The distinction between semantic consistency, homotopy canonicity and full normalization makes the selected operational guarantee substantive.

sentences: The selected question adds individual propositional resizing to a fixed univalent De Morgan cubical calculus.
Each homotopy proposition in one universe must have an equivalent representative in the adjacent smaller universe.
The requested result combines consistency with an algorithm that turns every closed natural-number derivation into a numeral and an object-theory path proof.
Existing canonicity theorems for the base calculus and models separating resizing principles do not establish this extension’s computational guarantee.
A resolution would clarify whether this useful size principle can retain effective natural-number observations without demanding full normalization.

definitions:
The base is the Cohen–Coquand–Huber–Mörtberg (CCHM) De Morgan cubical calculus, fixing the core syntax and judgmental computation rules of the cited7 November2016 version, §§2–7 and AppendixA, stratified over universe levels \(i\in\mathbb N\). Optional higher inductive types from its §9 are not included. The following conventions identify the object theory and its size/computation choices explicitly. Contexts contain typed term variables, interval names and face restrictions. There are dependent function types \(\prod_{x:A}B(x)\), dependent pair types \(\sum_{x:A}B(x)\), natural numbers with zero, successor and dependent recursion, dependent path types, cubical composition, Glue types and a cumulative Russell universe tower \(\mathcal U_i:\mathcal U_{i+1}\). A term \(A:\mathcal U_i\) is itself a type, with inclusion into higher levels. Each constructor is formed at the maximum universe level of its type arguments; the constructors and their computation rules are the same at every level. No universe contains itself.

Interval expressions are the finite terms freely generated by interval names, endpoints \(0,1\), meet, join and involution \(r\mapsto1-r\), modulo the bounded distributive lattice and De Morgan identities. They are not Boolean: \(r\lor(1-r)=1\) and \(r\land(1-r)=0\) are not added. Face formulas form the distributive lattice generated by equations \((i=0)\), \((i=1)\), with \((i=0)\land(i=1)\) false. A system is a finite collection of terms on faces covering a context, agreeing where faces overlap; on each face it computes to its indicated term. Substitution acts on term variables and interval expressions and preserves the face restrictions.

For a type family \(i:\mathbb I\vdash A(i)\), a dependent path with endpoints \(a_0:A(0)\) and \(a_1:A(1)\) is represented by an interval abstraction \(\langle i\rangle u\) with those boundary values; it can be applied at any interval expression. Path abstraction/application obey beta and eta, and application at an endpoint gives that endpoint. Write \(\mathsf{Path}_A(a,b)\) for the constant-family case. Composition \(\mathsf{comp}^i A[\varphi\mapsto u]a_0\) takes a partial line \(u\) on a face \(\varphi\) and a compatible starting point \(a_0:A(0)\), and produces an endpoint in \(A(1)\) agreeing with \(u(1)\) on that face. The fixed CCHM computation rules for composition on functions, pairs, natural numbers, paths, Glue types and universes are part of the base theory; they are not a variable to choose in an answer. Functions and pairs have their ordinary beta/eta conversions, and natural-number recursion has its zero and successor equations. Conversion is generated by these rules and congruence, not by reflection of arbitrary path proofs.

A Glue type \(\mathsf{Glue}[\varphi\mapsto(T,f)]A\) identifies a type \(A\) with a type \(T\) on a face, using an equivalence \(f:T\simeq A\) there. It has the CCHM glue/unglue introduction and elimination operations and their boundary/composition equations. Univalence in the base theory is the theorem that the canonical map from paths between universe elements to equivalences of the corresponding types is an equivalence. Paths therefore represent homotopical identity, rather than proof-irrelevant or extensional equality. There is no equality reflection, uniqueness-of-identity-proofs axiom, excluded-middle axiom or choice axiom in the object calculus.

For any type \(P\), define \[\mathsf{isProp}(P)=\prod_{x:P}\prod_{y:P}\mathsf{Path}_P(x,y).\] Such a type has at most one point up to homotopical identity; it can also be empty. Define \[\mathsf{isContr}(A)=\sum_{a:A}\prod_{x:A}\mathsf{Path}_A(a,x).\] For \(f:A\to B\), its fiber over \(b:B\) is \(\sum_{a:A}\mathsf{Path}_B(f(a),b)\); the assertion that \(f\) is an equivalence says every such fiber is contractible. The type \(A\simeq B\) consists of a function with this equivalence witness. These definitions are internal to the object calculus and use its paths.

The extension \(\mathsf T_R\) adds exactly the displayed typed constants \(R_i\), one at every adjacent universe pair, with their ordinary substitution instances. Applying \(R_i\) to a proposition and a witness of \(\mathsf{isProp}\) returns a smaller type together with an equivalence. That smaller type is then a proposition as a consequence of the equivalence. No judgmental equation for \(R_i\) is postulated. Thus the selected theorem is about effective homotopy canonicity of this fixed axiomatic extension; it does not presuppose a particular reduction rule for resizing or strengthen the requirement to judgmental canonicity. The scheme applies in arbitrary contexts, not only to closed propositions, and can be iterated across finitely many universe levels. It does not add an axiom that \[\Omega_i=\sum_{P:\mathcal U_i}\mathsf{isProp}(P)\] itself has size \(\mathcal U_i\); that is the separate whole-universe impredicativity principle distinguished by the source.

Finite syntax, universe indices, binders, systems and derivation trees have an ordinary explicit finite encoding; alpha-renaming does not change the mathematical judgments. Closed means that no free term variable or interval name remains. The numeral \(\overline k\) is \(\mathsf s^k0\). The required algorithm is a deterministic Turing-computable procedure with no oracle or advice. It receives the entire term and a finite derivation of its closed natural-number type. It returns \(k\), a finite term \(e\) and a finite derivation of the displayed path judgment in this same \(\mathsf T_R\), including any permitted resizing constants it uses. Its guarantee is for every valid input derivation and every finite universe level used in it. There is no time or output-length bound beyond termination; malformed inputs have no required mathematical output. A semantic equality unaccompanied by the required object-theory certificate is not the requested output.

Consistency is a separate requirement because an inconsistent calculus could manufacture arbitrary equality certificates. Specifically there must be no closed term identifying zero with its successor in the natural-number type; this is the usual numeral-separation test for this dependent calculus. Native Lean propositions, proof irrelevance or classical choice must not be substituted for the represented object-theory propositions, path judgments or computational procedure. Lean serves to check the metatheorem and the algorithm's guarantees.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof that the specified extension is consistent and admits the stated terminating numeral-and-path-certificate algorithm, or a complete Lean-checked refutation of this conjunction. A positive answer must supply a computable procedure and prove its termination and correctness for all closed natural-number derivations, including those using resizing at arbitrary finite levels. Consistency alone, existence of a classical semantic model, an unevaluated resizing postulate, or a canonicity theorem only for the base calculus is insufficient. A refutation must concern this resizing scheme and this effective homotopy requirement; showing that a particular reduction strategy gets stuck or that judgmental canonicity fails does not by itself refute it. No normalization theorem for all terms and no smallness axiom for the entire \(\Omega_i\) is additionally required. This is an exact existence question, not a numerical-value benchmark.

context_blocks.text: The source asks broadly for a computational interpretation of propositional impredicativity axioms. On16 September2026 the user selected individual resizing across adjacent universes, consistency and effective homotopy canonicity in a fixed univalent cubical theory. The card makes that specialization explicit and fixes the CCHM core plus the displayed resizing constants as the object calculus.

Resizing individual propositions and making the entire type of small propositions small are separate principles in the source and its published follow-up. The present target chooses the former. It does not use the word impredicativity to silently impose both.

Cubical type theory supplies computational structure for univalence. The base calculus manipulates paths through an interval, composition and gluing; its existing canonicity results concern that structure without the new resizing scheme. Adding a typed constant does not automatically preserve those theorems.

The 2022 work distinguishes judgmental canonicity from homotopy canonicity: a natural-number term can be path equal to a numeral even when it does not convert to that numeral by the stipulated equations. The selected target also asks for an effective procedure returning that numeral and its proof.

The published2025 domain-theory follow-up retains the broad computational-interpretation question. The 2025 POPL discussion likewise states that ordinary cubical propositional resizing lacks a known computational interpretation; its remarks about loss of canonicity on postulating an axiom are not taken as a proof against the weaker path-certificate target.

Uemura constructs a cubical-assembly model with a univalent impredicative universe while a propositional resizing principle fails in that model. This separates the semantic principles. It neither supplies the selected resizing computation nor proves that every possible computational account is impossible.

The desired certificate is an identity in the represented cubical theory. Its existence cannot be supplied by replacing every proposition with Lean’s proof-irrelevant Prop or by assuming a computational oracle for mathematical truth. The object theory and the ordinary algorithm are both part of the exact target.
